Defensive sectors can fall too, and their recent gains may unwind. Cash earns 0% and can lose purchasing power to inflation; there is no international equity exposure. The 14% drawdown estimate is not a loss limit.

theses.title: A soft landing is plausible, not bankable.
theses.worldView: My falsifiable 12-month base case is that U.S. real activity avoids a deep recession while inflation and interest-rate expectations remain uncertain; a deep contraction or a sustained inflation-driven rise in rates would disprove it.
theses.portfolioExpression: I hold 30% in zero-return cash, 25% in short-maturity Treasuries and 10% in broad bonds, limiting equities to 35% so the portfolio does not depend on either a boom or a large bond rally.

theses.title: Price discipline and resilient cash flows matter.
theses.worldView: SPY.US gained 13.5% over the supplied trailing year and closed about 3.4% below its 52-week high; I expect next-year equity returns to be choppier and to rely more on realized cash flows than on a further broad rerating. In a moderate slowdown, staples and healthcare demand should be relatively resilient; a deep demand shock or sustained growth-led market surge would challenge this view.
theses.portfolioExpression: The 35% equity sleeve combines broad U.S. exposure, a value tilt and small consumer-staples and healthcare allocations. Those funds also rose substantially over the supplied trailing year, so I size them modestly and do not treat price strength as proof of undervaluation.

pick.thesis: This fixed portfolio expresses a cautious middle-case view: 30% cash is a deliberate nominal buffer, not dry powder to be redeployed, while 35% bonds and 35% equities provide limited participation in income and economic growth. The supplied price history does not establish that any equity fund is intrinsically cheap, so value here means diversified, value-oriented or defensive exposure at a restrained portfolio weight, not a verified valuation discount.

forecasts.reason: If U.S. activity avoids a deep recession and rates do not rise sharply, limited equity exposure can participate in earnings and distributions while the bond funds provide income. The 30% zero-return cash allocation and restrained equity weight cap the plausible central gain; a recession or inflation shock could still produce a negative result, so +4% is an uncertain forecast rather than a guarantee.

positions.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF

positions.invalidation: A sustained rise in short rates or inflation could reduce market value or real returns, and the fund’s share price can fall despite its Treasury exposure.

positions.invalidation: Persistent inflation, rising yields or widening credit spreads could cause losses; an aggregate bond ETF is not a cash substitute.

positions.name: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF

positions.catalyst: Broad earnings and distributions holding up, with participation extending beyond a narrow set of market leaders, could support the fund.
positions.invalidation: A deep recession, a broad earnings decline or a sustained rise in rates that compresses equity valuations would undermine this application.

positions.name: Vanguard Value ETF

positions.catalyst: A market that rewards realized earnings and current cash flows, rather than sustained leadership from growth stocks, could benefit the value tilt.

positions.invalidation: Consumer trading-down, persistent input-cost pressure or competition that weakens margins could undermine the resilience thesis; the fund can still fall in a broad equity selloff.

positions.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund

Its value here is sector diversification and exposure to ongoing healthcare needs, not a verified discount, and a 5% weight recognizes both the recent advance and sector-specific risks.
positions.catalyst: Steady medical demand and continued conversion of healthcare innovation into broad-sector cash flows could support returns.
positions.invalidation: Regulatory or reimbursement pressure, weaker sector cash flows or a broad rise in discount rates could invalidate the resilience case and reduce fund value.

GOOG.US and ADBE.US both face technology disruption risk, while NKE.US depends on discretionary demand and brand relevance. theses.title: Uneven growth favors current cash flows
theses.worldView: Over the next 12 months, my base case is positive but uneven activity rather than a synchronized deep recession or a smooth, durable collapse in real financing costs; established businesses with current cash generation should therefore be more resilient than assets priced mainly on distant growth. A broad earnings contraction or a durable easing-led regime in which long-duration growth persistently dominates would falsify this view.
theses.portfolioExpression: I make a broad US value-style ETF the largest equity holding and add a modest, diversified capital allocator. This expresses a preference for current business value, not a claim that the supplied market data proves current valuations are cheap.

theses.title: Global breadth remains investable
theses.worldView: Over the horizon, developed and emerging economies avoid a synchronized severe recession and non-US markets participate in global returns. A deep foreign earnings downturn or persistent currency and earnings headwinds that drive continued relative deterioration would falsify this view.
theses.portfolioExpression: EFA.US and VWO.US provide a measured allocation to developed and emerging markets outside the US, diversifying country and currency exposure without making a foreign-market rebound essential to the portfolio.

theses.title: Digital utility survives interface change
theses.worldView: Generative AI and cloud competition will change online search and creative-software workflows over the next 12 months, but will not erase the economic utility of established internet and productivity platforms. Widespread customer migration or sustained monetization erosion would falsify this claim.
theses.portfolioExpression: Modest GOOG.US and ADBE.US holdings express the possibility that recent price declines overstate disruption, while keeping those uncertain outcomes subordinate to diversified funds.

theses.title: Household spending is selective, not absent
theses.worldView: Over the next year, household spending is uneven: essential goods remain relatively resilient while discretionary brands must earn demand and may be repriced sharply. A broad consumption recession or continuing loss of relevance across established brands would falsify this view.
theses.portfolioExpression: XLP.US supplies diversified essentials exposure, while NKE.US is only a small contrarian application; its price decline is evidence of changed expectations, not proof of mispricing.

theses.title: Rate paths remain uncertain
theses.worldView: Inflation, growth and funding surprises leave a meaningful possibility of interest-rate volatility over the next year. Rising yields can hurt bonds, while smooth disinflation and falling yields can make cash and short-duration holdings lag equities; a calm rate environment in which the buffer's opportunity cost dominates would weaken this thesis.
theses.portfolioExpression: I hold 10% SHY.US, 8% BND.US and 12% zero-return cash, deliberately sacrificing some upside to reduce dependence on a single equity scenario.

pick.thesis: The fixed portfolio expresses uneven growth, current cash-flow value and broader international participation while allowing for persistent rate uncertainty. It holds 70% equities, including a 23% value-style core and 15% in international funds; GOOG.US, ADBE.US and NKE.US together are only 18%, so no single disruption or turnaround outcome drives the book. The remaining 18% is in bond funds and 12% in cash. Weights are held unchanged for the full horizon.

forecasts.reason: An 8% expected total return is a modest positive base case, not an extrapolation of the supplied 13.5% trailing 12-month SPY.US return. It is plausible if activity avoids a deep recession, value and international holdings participate, the small digital and consumer positions stabilize, and bond income accrues. Renewed inflation or rate shocks, AI-driven disruption or a global earnings downturn could instead make the realized return negative.

positions.invalidation: If new interfaces displace search queries at scale, advertising economics weaken or regulation impairs distribution, the digital-demand thesis may not translate into shareholder returns.

positions.thesis: Applied Materials sells semiconductor-fabrication equipment; at $370.55 on 2026-11-09 it was 48.7% below its 52-week high, but still 59.6% above its 12-month-ago level after a 29.4% three-month fall. I view the volatility as a possible cyclical-reset entry if fab investment persists, not proof of a low valuation, and cap the weight at 16% because equipment spending is highly cyclical.
positions.catalyst: A sustained resumption in leading-edge, memory and packaging equipment orders would make this correction look cyclical.
positions.invalidation: Several years of fab-capital-spending cuts, export restrictions or technology shifts that bypass its tools would make the decline an earnings reset rather than an opportunity.

positions.name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
positions.thesis: Taiwan Semiconductor is a contract foundry for chip designers; the $388.62 close was 20.0% below its $485.80 52-week high after a 35.8% 12-month gain and a 7.7% three-month decline. Continuing global compute demand would support the value of scale-intensive manufacturing capacity after this pullback, but the trailing gain means the packet cannot establish that it is cheap, so the weight is limited to 12%.
positions.catalyst: Continued outsourced demand for advanced processes and healthy utilization, especially if cloud and AI chip volumes broaden, could support a re-rating.
positions.invalidation: A Taiwan military crisis, material customer insourcing, competitor gains or a prolonged chip downcycle would override the demand thesis.

positions.name: Oracle
positions.thesis: Oracle sells enterprise database and business software and has a cloud-infrastructure business; its $119.79 close was 51.4% below the $246.38 52-week high and 50.2% lower over 12 months, near the packet's $114.57 low. If businesses keep expanding cloud workloads and Oracle can monetize them, the repricing may offer a contrarian entry into an installed software base, but it could also reflect durable execution or financing concerns, so the weight is 10%.
positions.catalyst: Cloud and database workloads translating into recurring cash generation rather than just additional spending could demonstrate the thesis.
positions.invalidation: If capital needs or financing costs outrun monetized cloud growth, or enterprises materially move away from its database and software base, the low price may be justified.

positions.name: Bank of America
positions.thesis: Bank of America is a large U.S. deposit, lending and payments bank; the $50.55 close was 21.6% below the $64.48 52-week high, down 20.6% over three months and 3.1% over 12 months. Under the soft-landing thesis, continued household and business activity with contained credit losses could allow the market to revalue the franchise after a sharp selloff; without current book-value or credit data, this remains a conditional 10% recovery position.
positions.catalyst: An orderly economy, stable credit losses and improved rate or funding conditions could restore confidence in bank earnings.
positions.invalidation: A recession with rising charge-offs, costly deposit competition or sustained margin compression would undermine the recovery case.

positions.name: Nike
positions.thesis: Nike designs and sells global athletic footwear and apparel; at $39.88 it was 39.6% below its $66.04 52-week high and down 33.4% over 12 months. If consumer demand and product execution normalize, its global brand could offer meaningful recovery potential at this reset, but price weakness does not prove that the brand has bottomed, so the allocation is 8%.
positions.catalyst: Sustained full-price consumer demand and improved product execution could restore brand pricing power.
positions.invalidation: Continued market-share loss, structurally weak product relevance, prolonged discounting or a consumer recession would defeat the recovery thesis.

positions.name: Constellation Energy
positions.thesis: Constellation Energy is a U.S. power generator with substantial nuclear-generation exposure; the $276.09 close was 26.7% below the $376.93 52-week high and 21.0% below its 12-month-ago level. If reliable electricity becomes more valuable as compute and electrification loads grow, existing generation could benefit from scarcity, but the price data cannot establish earnings or valuation, so this is an 8% satellite.
positions.catalyst: Growing demand for dependable generation or tighter local supply could improve realized power economics.
positions.invalidation: Flat load, rapid new supply, sustained lower power prices, unfavorable market rules or prolonged plant outages could break the supply-scarcity link.

positions.name: SPDR Gold Shares
positions.thesis: SPDR Gold Shares is a bullion fund rather than a cash-generating business; at $379.53 it was 23.5% below its $495.90 52-week high, up 3.7% over 12 months and down 5.3% over three months. Gold could hedge the portfolio if real rates fall or financial and geopolitical stress rises, but it is not an intrinsically cheap equity, so its allocation is kept at 8%.
positions.catalyst: Lower real yields, renewed inflation concern or financial and geopolitical stress could revive bullion demand.
positions.invalidation: Persistently rising real yields and a strong dollar with calm markets could leave non-yielding gold under pressure.

pick.knowledgeLimitations: The frozen packet ends on 2026-11-09 and supplies adjusted prices, trailing returns and 52-week ranges, but no contemporaneous financial statements, valuation multiples, guidance, balance sheets, news or explanations for price moves. I use the high-to-current price declines as evidence of price dislocation, not proof of intrinsic value. Business descriptions reflect general knowledge, and the macro theses and catalysts remain uncertain assumptions.

strategies.riskRationale: This fixed 24-month portfolio puts 82% in equities, including 56% in correlated compute and platform exposures, accepting substantial drawdown risk for rerating upside. I estimate a roughly 40% peak-to-trough decline is plausible; gold and cash may soften losses but will not control them.
